sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: In lesson 12 you said what you did: I cleaned, I went. Now you'll learn to ask about the past — «did you clean the kitchen?» —, to say «not» — «I didn't buy the shoes» — and to tell a story in order: «first of all… then… in the end».

examples.translation: You ask if the kitchen is clean now.
I left the shoes in the shop.

examples.en: First of all, I checked the address.
examples.translation: The first thing I did was check it.

examples.en: In the end, I took the bus.
examples.translation: After everything, I took the bus.

blocks.text: Make the question like in lesson 7, but use Did instead of Do or Does — and Did is the same for everyone: Did you…? Did she…? After Did, the action is as in the dictionary, with no -ed: Did you clean, not Did you cleaned.

examples.translation: You ask if the kitchen is clean now.

examples.en: Did you wash the coffee mug?
examples.translation: You ask if the mug is clean.

examples.en: Did she wash the tea strainer?
examples.translation: You ask if she cleaned the tea strainer.
You ask if they ate a fig.
You ask if they visited famous places.

fixes.wrong: Does she wash the tea strainer yesterday?
fixes.right: Did she wash the tea strainer yesterday?

drill.why: Did already shows the past, so the action is as in the dictionary.

blocks.text: To say «not» about the past, put didn't before the action — the same for everyone. Again, the action is as in the dictionary: I didn't buy, not I didn't bought. Only did shows the past.

examples.translation: I left the shoes in the shop.
I stayed sitting or standing.
I went out.
I came back late.

examples.en: I didn't fill in the form.
examples.translation: The form is still empty.

fixes.wrong: I don't buy the shoes yesterday.
fixes.right: I didn't buy the shoes yesterday.

drill.hint: One word is in the wrong form. Tap it.
drill.fix: After didn't, the action is as in the dictionary: I didn't buy the shoes.

blocks.text: The main rule of the lesson: show the past in one place only. Either in the action (I cleaned) or in did (Did you clean? I didn't clean). Not twice: Did you cleaned is wrong.

examples.translation: The past is in «cleaned».
The past is in «Did».
The past is in «didn't».
The past is in «Did».

drill.question: You ask your friend if they drove more slowly. Which is correct?
drill.explain: The past is already in Did, so slow has no -ed.

blocks.text: Many English actions are two words: pick up, put away, run out of, slow down. The second word changes the meaning, so you can't drop it.

examples.en: Did you pick up the parcel?
examples.translation: Did you collect the parcel?

examples.en: Did you put away the clothes?
examples.translation: Did you put the clothes in their place?

examples.en: Did you run out of milk?
examples.translation: Is there no milk left?

examples.en: I didn't give back the book.
examples.translation: I still have the book.
I stayed on my feet.

fixes.right: Did you run out of milk?

blocks.text: Learn these actions as a whole — both words together, like one new word.
Questions and «not» about the past often come with a time: yesterday, afterwards (after that), beforehand (before, early). These words go at the end.

examples.translation: Was your call yesterday?
Did you call after that?

examples.en: Did you buy the tickets beforehand?
examples.translation: Did you buy them early, before the day?

examples.en: Did you move in last week?
examples.translation: Did you start living there last week?

fixes.wrong: Did you buy beforehand the tickets?
fixes.right: Did you buy the tickets beforehand?

blocks.text: To show you're sure or how you feel: definitely, certainly, luckily. definitely and certainly go before the action; luckily goes at the start.

examples.translation: I'm sure I called yesterday.
Of course I paid yesterday.
I was lucky — I got on the bus in time.

sections.title: In order: First of all, Then, In the end

blocks.text: To tell a story step by step: First of all, At first, Then, In the end. They go at the start. Careful: for «finally, after everything», say In the end, not At the end.

examples.en: First of all, I checked the address.
examples.translation: The first thing I did was check it.
In the beginning, I waited outside.

examples.en: Then we stopped off at a café.
examples.translation: After that we visited a café for a short time.

examples.en: In the end, I took the bus.
examples.translation: After everything, I took the bus.

drill.why: «Finally, after everything» is In the end.

blocks.text: Words ending in -ly say how something was done: politely, patiently, kindly. They go after the action and the thing: Did she wait patiently?

examples.translation: Did she ask in a nice, polite way?
Did she wait calmly, without getting angry?
Did she speak in a kind way?

fixes.right: Did you run out of milk?

fixes.wrong: At the end, I took the bus.
fixes.right: In the end, I took the bus.

blocks.text: If there's did or didn't, the action is as in the dictionary. If there's no did, the action has -ed or is a special word. Show the past only once.
Questions about the past: Did + who + action as in the dictionary. «Not»: didn't + action as in the dictionary. Two-word actions: learn them whole. Telling a story: First of all, Then, In the end.

examples.translation: You ask if they ate a nectarine.

examples.en: I didn't save up for a bike.
examples.translation: I didn't keep money for a bike.
Did you start your trip early?

examples.en: In the end, I took the bus.
examples.translation: After everything, I took the bus.
